images.filename: Adana Yağ Camii Exterior Courtyard in 2008 58 3568.jpg
images.caption:
The Yağ Camii or Oil Mosque is situated in a former church (but extended), as can be seen from the outside of its courtyard. Entrance to that courtyard is through a monumental gate, the mosque is opposite and to the right of the entrance. To the left of the entrance there is a medrese, other sides have facilities. It used to be an oasis of quiet in a busy neighbourhood, as the çarşı (markets- , shopping) area is around, and the street passing it has a continuous stream of dolmuses and other traffic. The mosque itself is plain. Due to restorations the complex looks brand new, but its well over half a millennium old. 
View from roughly in front of the medrese.

images.filename: Adana Archaeological Museum Achilles' Sarcophagus 170-190 AD 0456.jpg
images.caption: This sarcophagus is of the second group of Achilles tombs of Attica type from the Roman Imperial Period. The left and short façade an its front façade are allocated to the figures. There is a sphinx in the right short face and opposing Gryphons on its rear long façade. Although the work bears the characteristics of the Late Antonines period, it may be dated to between AD 170 and 190.
images.alt: This sarcophagus is of the second group of Achilles tombs of Attica type from the Roman Imperial Period. The left and short façade an its front façade are allocated to the figures. images.filename: Adana Hasan Ağa Mosque Interior underside balcony in 2008 5720.jpg
images.caption:
The Hasan Ağa mosque is also known as the Hasan Kethüda, it is situated in the area to the West of the Yağ Camii and dates from 1558. It has been built by Abdullah Hasan Ağa during the reign of the Ramazanoğlu ruler Pir Bey. It is special in that it is the only mosque in Adana in the classical Ottoman style (though the Merkez mosque is in that very style, but modern). It was damaged in an 27 June 1998 earthquake, and was back at work in 2004.
Inside there was a fine woodwork balcony over the entrance, I was told there was an alternation of motiveless panels and some 11 different motives.

images.caption: A Roman Catholic church, called the Bebekli Church (Church with child) with about 150 believers and a young priest from Bangalore (ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು). The church was built in 1880 and is dedicated to Saint Paul. The statue of the Virgin Mary on top is made of bronze. It was seen as representing a child, hence the name of the church. Since it is the only church in town (at least at the time the picture was taken) it is visited by people from other Christian denominations also.

images.caption:
This is the Ağca Masjid, the oldest religious building in Adana, built under Ağca Bey in 1489. In 1770 it was restored thoroughly under Hacı Hasan Ağa. It resembles a türbe from the outside. It was damaged in an 27 June 1998 earthquake, and was back at work in 2004. The building is quite close to the Ulu Camii.
The building has nice decoration in stone on the inside as well as the outside.

images.caption: A notice pictured in 2008 stated, translated: “Green Mosque. The Green Mosque was built by the Gencizade family. It takes its name from the green color of the dome covering the space. Made of yellow tufa stone, the building, with its square plan and single-domed space, is one of the commonly seen mosques. It was restored by the General Directorate of Foundations in 1965 and reopened for worship.” In later years a sentence in English claims the mescit (a smallish mosque or prayer room) was built in 1751 (and another restoration ending in 2005). I passed it often in a region where I often walked, but never found it open.  So just lots of pictures of its details.
